built_pages_note: Measured 2026-09-06 (paper lap 12) by paper/measure_pages.py on this lap's own build: 23 pages under Carlito, page objects and page-tree /Count agreeing, gated by check_paper.py against the author's 25-page rule (NH-028). It was 23 at lap 11 too, and lap 12 added 144 body words (8,825 -> 8,969) without buying a page - which is the curve behaving as paper/README.md's table says it does between 8,561 and 8,961 words, not a lap getting something for nothing. THE PAGE MARGIN AND THE WORD MARGIN NOW DISAGREE SHARPLY: two pages under the author's rule, 31 words under the 9,000-word proxy. The proxy is the tighter of the two by about a thousand words (paper/README.md, 'How many pages this actually is'), so the next lap that must ship a caveat will be stopped by the proxy and not by the rule the author actually set. That is escalated as NH-037 and it is the one thing about this file a reader should carry away. THE FACE IS PART OF THE NUMBER: metric-compatible Carlito stands in for the non-redistributable Calibri build_docx.py asks for, so the gate reports and falls back to the 9,000-word proxy on any face whose metrics are not Calibri's. This lap could measure only because it ran the apt line paper/README.md records; a clean clone still cannot, which is WFG-116's open half. F9_present_perimeter is still drawn, committed and NOT referenced by the manuscript (paper/GAPS.md, gap G8, NH-032 open), so it still costs no page here and will cost one when it is referenced. built_pages_inputs is the WFG-116 anchor: the digest of the document this 23 was measured on (the ordered figure list with pixel sizes, the table and reference counts, the body-word count). It does NOT re-derive the page count and nothing in this file does. Set both fields to null rather than hand-writing an anchor no run produced.
